blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Customs and duties are often treated as an operational cost, quietly absorbed by the trade team and invisible to strategy. That view is dated. In the current environment, tariffs are increasingly used as instruments of foreign policy, and changes announced in capitals can reshape entire trade flows within weeks.

A sophisticated customs strategy rests on three foundations. The first is real-time intelligence: tariff changes, regulatory updates and origin rules must be monitored at the level of headline and footnote, not just headline. The second is classification rigour: HS codes, origin declarations, and valuation methods must be consistent, defensible, and reviewed regularly, because even small errors compound into large liabilities. The third is optionality: where possible, the sourcing and routing of goods should be structured to allow a credible, low-friction response if trade rules shift suddenly.

The unspoken truth is that customs, once a clerical matter, has rejoined the main table of corporate strategy. Companies that accept this early adjust quickly. Companies that resist it are told, eventually, by their numbers.

items.q: According to the text, how are customs and duties often treated?
options: As the central concern of the board
As a source of competitive advantage
As a purely legal question for counsel
As an operational cost invisible to strategy
items.why: "Customs and duties are often treated as an operational cost… invisible to strategy."

items.q: What are the three foundations of a sophisticated customs strategy?
options: Real-time intelligence, classification rigour and optionality
items.why: "three foundations. The first is real-time intelligence… The second is classification rigour… The third is optionality."

items.q: Why must small classification errors be taken seriously?
options: They slow down the shipping process
They damage the company's public reputation
items.why: "even small errors compound into large liabilities."

items.q: What does the phrase "Companies that resist it are told, eventually, by their numbers" most likely suggest?
options: Ignoring the shift eventually shows up as damage in the financials
The numbers always favour companies that wait
Resistant companies will be audited by regulators
Strategy should be decided by the finance team alone
items.why: Inferência: quem ignora a mudança acaba pagando — o prejuízo aparece nos resultados financeiros.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Customs deserves a place in corporate strategy
Tariffs can be used as tools of foreign policy
Monitoring should extend to the footnotes, not just headlines
Customs is a routine clerical function best left off the strategy table
items.why: Inferência: a tese central é que alfândega deixou de ser assunto burocrático e voltou à mesa da estratégia.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte informando a liderança sobre as novas tarifas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me set out where we stand. The tariffs announced last week land squarely on our two main corridors, and I want everyone to understand the exposure before we react.

On the eastern corridor, roughly forty per cent of our volume is now subject to a duty that did not exist a fortnight ago. The measure was framed as a policy response, not a revenue one, which tells me it can be escalated or withdrawn with very little notice. So I would not treat the current rate as a stable planning number.

On the southern corridor, the headline rate barely moved, but a footnote changed the origin rules. Read carefully, it means several of our components no longer qualify for the preferential treatment we have been claiming. If our classification is challenged, the back-duty could be significant.

Here is my recommendation. We do not rush to re-route everything this week. Instead, we build optionality: we qualify a second supplier on each corridor, we tighten our origin declarations, and we hold enough flexibility to move volume within days if the rules shift again. What I am asking you to sign off on today is the principle — that customs is now a strategic variable, not a cost we quietly absorb.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What has happened on the eastern corridor?
options: A supplier has withdrawn from the route
The corridor has been closed entirely
Around forty per cent of volume now faces a new duty
Volumes have doubled since last week
items.why: "roughly forty per cent of our volume is now subject to a duty that did not exist a fortnight ago."

items.q: Why does Charlotte refuse to treat the current eastern rate as a stable planning number?
options: Because it applies only to a single product line
Because the finance team has not yet approved it
Because it was framed as a policy measure, which can change with little notice
Because the calculation is disputed by auditors
items.why: Inferência: sendo instrumento de política, pode ser escalada ou retirada a qualquer momento — logo, instável.

items.q: What actually changed on the southern corridor?
options: A footnote altered the origin rules, disqualifying some components
The route was rerouted through a third country
The corridor gained a new preferential agreement
items.why: "the headline rate barely moved, but a footnote changed the origin rules."

items.q: What is Charlotte's core recommendation?
options: Absorb the duties quietly as before
Re-route all volume immediately this week
Build optionality — second suppliers, tighter declarations, flexibility to move fast
Suspend both corridors until the rules settle
items.why: "we build optionality: we qualify a second supplier on each corridor, we tighten our origin declarations…"

items.q: What is Charlotte ultimately asking the team to accept?
options: That customs is a strategic variable, not just a cost to absorb
That the trade team should be reorganised
That the eastern corridor should be abandoned
That tariffs will always be temporary
items.why: "What I am asking you to sign off on today is the principle — that customs is now a strategic variable."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The new tariff lands on forty per cent of our volume." A tariff is…
options: a tax imposed on imported or exported goods
items.why: Tariff = tarifa: imposto cobrado sobre bens importados ou exportados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A footnote changed the ___, so several components no longer qualify for preferential treatment."
items.why: Origin rules = regras de origem: determinam se um bem se qualifica para tratamento preferencial.

items.q: "Even small errors compound into large liabilities." Here, to compound means to…
items.why: To compound = acumular-se: pequenos erros vão se somando até virarem um passivo grande.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If our classification is challenged, the back-duty becomes a serious ___ on the balance sheet."
items.why: Liability = passivo: uma obrigação financeira que pesa no balanço.

items.q: Optionality, as used in the lesson, is best described as…
options: the option to opt out of customs entirely
the number of tariff codes available
the built-in flexibility to respond credibly if the rules shift
items.why: Optionality = opcionalidade: estruturar sourcing e rotas para poder reagir rápido quando as regras mudam.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre política de comércio e alfândega. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new customs strategy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new origin declarations corridor by corridor." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two country managers pushed back on the re-routing plan." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to tighten classification but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Absorbing the duty quietly will not move the needle on our exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
